# Boldface

> Boldface is a LinkedIn agency based in Bangalore, India, for founders, CEOs, CFOs, consultants and executives. It runs LinkedIn end to end: profile and positioning, ghostwritten posts, newsletters, strategic networking, collaborations and events, company pages and leadership teams, plus one-off audits and workshops. Clients are across India, Dubai and Abu Dhabi, with others in the UK and Singapore.

Key facts:
- Founded and led by Koushik Agarwalla (curator and execution lead), who plans, writes and runs every engagement. Brand strategy advisor: Sandeep Komarla (former AVP Disney Star, Senior Director Viacom18, Marketing Head Radio City).
- 35+ founders, CEOs and executives worked with over four years; 265K+ followers built and 55M+ organic impressions across clients.
- Pricing: Monthly retainers start from ₹15,000 to ₹18,000 a month, depending on scope. Larger engagements are priced on a call.
- Engagements are monthly retainers with 30 days' notice. No lock-in.
- Every post is written in the client's voice and approved by the client before it goes out. Clients typically spend under 30 minutes a week.
- Networking is done by hand. Boldface never uses LinkedIn automation tools or engagement pods.
- First call to first post in 21 days.
- Boldface does not offer traditional PR or press pitching; it focuses entirely on LinkedIn.
- Contact: koushik@boldface.click, WhatsApp +91 70772 47111, book a free 30 minute call at https://calendly.com/boldfaceonline/30min

## Services
- [LinkedIn Profile Optimisation](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-profile-optimisation/): LinkedIn profile optimisation done properly: positioning, headline, About, Featured and experience rewritten so the right people get you in ten seconds. For founders and leaders in India and the UAE.
- [LinkedIn Ghostwriting and Content Management](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-ghostwriting/): LinkedIn ghostwriting for founders, CEOs and executives: 8 to 12 posts a month in your voice, plus carousels, short video and articles. Planned, written, designed and posted for you.
- [LinkedIn Newsletter Management](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-newsletter-management/): We name, set up, plan, write and grow your LinkedIn newsletter. Every issue in your voice, published on schedule, with subscriber growth built in. For founders and executives.
- [Strategic LinkedIn Networking](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-networking/): Strategic LinkedIn networking done by people, not bots: a target list of investors, buyers and partners, personal connection notes, thoughtful comments and DM replies drafted for you.
- [LinkedIn Collaborations, Lives and Events](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-collaborations/): Grow on LinkedIn by borrowing the right audiences: co-written posts with peers, podcast and LinkedIn Live guest spots, LinkedIn events and paid brand partnerships, set up and run for you.
- [LinkedIn Company Page Management](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-company-page-management/): LinkedIn company page management that works through your people: page content and growth, leadership team profiles and posts, and employee posts made easy to share. One story across every account.
- [LinkedIn Audit and Workshops](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-audit/): A LinkedIn audit of your profile and content with a written fix list ranked by impact, or a hands-on LinkedIn workshop for your leadership team. For people who'd rather do it themselves.

The problem

Somebody looked you up before your last big meeting. They found a job title, three reshared posts and a profile photo from 2019. Meanwhile, someone less qualified got the keynote, the partnership and the investor's attention. Not because they're better. Because they're easier to find.

It lists where you've worked. It says nothing about how you think, and that's the only thing anyone is buying.

The investor, the buyer, the partner you want. They're on LinkedIn every day, and you've never once been in their feed.

- 03
### The deal went quiet after they looked you up.
Nobody tells you it happened. You just never hear back.

### You posted for a month. Crickets.
Good ideas, no system behind them. That part is fixable.

Honest filter
## We turn down morework than we take.

We keep the client list short on purpose. Read both columns before you book.

### Good fit Yes

- You have something real to say: a business, a career, a hard-won opinion.

- You can wait six months for the good stuff.

- You want a strategy, not a posting schedule.

- You're fine being told a draft isn't good enough yet.

- You care what people think of you in five years, not five days.

### Not a fit No

- You want 10,000 followers by next month.

- You're choosing on price alone.

- You want to sound like everyone else, just louder.

- You can't find 30 minutes to get your own voice right.

- You think personal branding is vanity.

Quick answers

01

**Q: What does “everything on LinkedIn” actually mean?**

Five things. We fix your profile so it says what you want to be known for. We write and publish your posts and newsletter. We build your network on purpose, one relevant person at a time. We set up collaborations: co-written posts, podcasts, Lives and brand partnerships. And for companies, we run the page and get the leadership team posting too.

02

**Q: How long before LinkedIn brings in real inbound?**

Engagement usually picks up in four to six weeks. Real conversations tend to start between months three and six. A genuine shift in how your industry sees you takes six to twelve months. Anyone promising faster is selling follower counts.

03

**Q: What does it cost?**

It's a monthly retainer, scoped to what you need: one piece, like a newsletter, or your whole LinkedIn. Get on a 30-minute call and we'll give you an actual number.

Services

# Everything on LinkedIn, handled.

Seven ways in. Most clients start with one or two and add the rest once it's working. Either way, senior people do the work, and nothing goes out without your sign-off.

01 [Profile & Positioning](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-profile-optimisation/)
## Look like the person you actually are.

Most profiles read like a CV. Yours should read like a point of view. We work out what you want to be known for and who needs to know it, then rebuild every part of your profile around that, so a stranger gets it in ten seconds.

- Positioning: what you stand for and who it's for
- Headline, About, Featured and experience rewritten
- Banner and profile photo direction
- Profile audit, also available on its own
02 [Content & Ghostwriting](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-ghostwriting/)
## Your LinkedIn, written and run for you.

We plan it, write it in your voice, design it, post it and adjust based on what's working. Text posts, carousels, short videos cut from footage you shoot on your phone, and long-form articles. You approve. That's about it.

- Monthly content plan and calendar
- 8 to 12 posts a month, written in your voice
- Carousels and document posts
- Short video edited from your own footage
- LinkedIn articles for longer thinking
03 [Newsletter Management](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-newsletter-management/)
## A newsletter people actually open.

A LinkedIn newsletter reaches people through notifications and email, not just the feed, and LinkedIn invites your network to subscribe when it launches. We name it, set it up, plan the issues, write every one in your voice and grow the list.

- Name, format and setup
- Editorial calendar
- Every issue written and published
- Subscriber growth
- Issue by issue review
04 [Strategic Networking](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-networking/)
## The right people, on purpose.

Posting gets you seen. Networking gets you in the room. We build a list of the people who matter to you, from investors and buyers to partners and peers, and work it every week. They see your name in their comments long before your message reaches their inbox.

- A target list of people worth knowing
- Personal connection notes, never templates
- Thoughtful comments on their posts
- DM replies drafted for you
- No automation tools, ever
05 [Collaborations & Events](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-collaborations/)
## Borrow the right audiences.

The fastest way to grow on LinkedIn is to show up where your audience already is. We set up co-written posts with peers, guest spots on podcasts and LinkedIn Lives, events of your own and, if brands want your audience, paid partnerships we source and negotiate for you.

- Co-written posts with peers
- Podcast and LinkedIn Live guest spots
- LinkedIn Lives, audio events and Events, run for you
- Brand partnerships, sourced and negotiated
06 [Company Pages & Teams](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-company-page-management/)
## The company, seen through its people.

People follow people before they follow logos. We run your company page and get your leadership team posting too, each in their own voice, all telling one story. Employees can join in with posts we make easy to share.

- Company page content and growth
- Leadership team profiles and posts
- Employee posts made easy to share
- One story across every account
07 [Audits & Workshops](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-audit/)
## Rather do it yourself? Start here.

Not everyone needs us every month. Some people need a sharp outside eye once. We audit your profile and content and hand you a ranked fix list, or train your leadership team in a single working session.

- Profile and content audit
- A written fix list, ranked by impact
- LinkedIn workshop for leadership teams

# Page: Case Studies | LinkedIn Results for Founders and Executives | Boldface
URL: https://boldface.online/work/

Work

# Ten clients, start to finish.

Ten engagements, told straight. Client names are withheld at their request. They'd rather you saw the results than their logo.

### Case study: Fintech founder, Mumbai
01 Fintech founder, Mumbai From 400 followers to a credible founder voice on LinkedIn LinkedIn Management + PR 12,000 LinkedIn Followers 12,000 LinkedIn Followers 9 Months 3 Media Features
A fintech founder from Mumbai came to us with 400 LinkedIn followers and a desire to build a credible public voice in his industry. He had been posting occasionally but with no strategy, no consistency and no real sense of what he was trying to communicate beyond general business content. His profile was functional but generic. The headline read like a job description. The About section was written in third person and read like a press release.

The first thing we worked on was positioning. What was his specific point of view on fintech? Not what his company did, but what he believed about the industry, where it was going and what most people were getting wrong. After two sessions and a lot of back and forth, we arrived at something specific enough to be useful: a clear perspective on why most fintech products fail at distribution, not at technology. That became the anchor for everything.

Over the next nine months, we published eight to ten posts per month, all written in his voice, all anchored to that core positioning. We also pitched his founder story to relevant publications. Within four months, he had earned three media features. The combination of consistent LinkedIn content and earned media created a compounding effect. By month six, journalists were reaching out to him instead of the other way around.

The most meaningful outcome was not the follower count. It was that the right people in his industry now recognised his name and his point of view before they ever spoke to him. His exact words: "People come into conversations already knowing how I think. That changes everything."
LinkedIn Management PR

### Case study: HR tech founder, Bangalore
02 HR tech founder, Bangalore Building enterprise credibility for a B2B SaaS founder LinkedIn Management + PR + Content Strategy 3 Major Media Features 3 Major Media Features 4 Months 5,000 Followers Built
The founder of a B2B HR tech company from Bangalore had a strong product and a growing client list, but a LinkedIn profile that did nothing for her credibility. She had 1,200 followers accumulated over several years, almost no engagement, and a posting cadence of roughly once a month when she had time. Her target buyers were heads of HR and CHROs at mid-size companies. The problem was that when those buyers looked her up, they did not find the kind of digital presence that signals expertise and trustworthiness.

We started by completely rebuilding her positioning. She had deep expertise in how HR technology actually gets adopted inside organisations, not just how it gets sold. That was the specific angle we built her content around: the implementation realities that vendors never talk about, the reasons most HR tech deployments fail and what actually works. This perspective was credible because it came from running implementations at her own company. It was also distinctive because almost nobody in her space was saying it.

The PR work ran parallel to the LinkedIn strategy. We pitched her as an expert source on technology adoption inside enterprise HR functions. Within four months, she had earned three media features. The LinkedIn content gave journalists confidence that she had interesting things to say. The media coverage gave her LinkedIn audience third-party validation of her expertise.

The visibility impact was clear. Within six months, the right buyers in her space recognised her as a credible voice, and conversations were easier because they had already formed a positive opinion of her before the first call.
LinkedIn Management PR Content Strategy

### Case study: Chartered accountant turned consultant, Delhi
03 Chartered accountant turned consultant, Delhi Building an inbound consulting pipeline from scratch LinkedIn Management + Personal Branding 6,500 LinkedIn Followers 6,500 LinkedIn Followers 6 Months 2-4 Inbound / week
A chartered accountant with twelve years of experience at Big Four firms had recently left to set up his own advisory practice in Delhi. His entire business model until that point had been built on referrals and on the credibility of the firm name behind him. On his own, he had a blank LinkedIn profile, no content presence and no way for potential clients to find him other than through the people who already knew him.

The challenge with building a personal brand in professional services, particularly in accounting and tax, is that the category is seen as technical rather than conversational. Most CA profiles on LinkedIn read like resumes. Most posts in the space are either regulatory updates or generic business advice. Neither positions anyone as someone worth paying a premium to work with.

We built his positioning around a specific gap he had identified from his Big Four experience: the vast majority of founders and promoters of mid-size Indian companies are underserved on tax and financial strategy because their advisors are either too junior to give strategic advice or too expensive to be accessible. He was the exception: Big Four quality, independent flexibility, accessible to founders who actually need strategic thinking, not just compliance.

The content strategy reflected this positioning directly. We wrote weekly posts on topics like structuring decisions at the growth stage, common financial-planning mistakes founders make, and how to think about strategic finance when you cannot yet afford a full-time CFO. Within two months, the engagement was consistent and growing. Within six months, he had built a 6,500-follower audience and was receiving two to four qualified inbound inquiries per week. Just as importantly, the people reaching out already understood the value he offered.
LinkedIn Management Personal Branding

### Case study: D2C skincare brand founder, Gurgaon
04 D2C skincare brand founder, Gurgaon Turning a founder's story into brand awareness at scale LinkedIn Management + PR + Personal Branding 4 Media Features 4 Media Features 8,000 LinkedIn Followers 2 Industry Panels
A founder from Gurgaon had built a D2C skincare brand over three years, growing it to a mid-size direct-to-consumer business entirely through paid acquisition and word of mouth. The brand was well-regarded within its customer base but had almost no public presence. The founder herself was completely invisible online: no LinkedIn content, no press coverage, no personal profile to speak of.

The brief was to change that. Not to promote the brand directly, but to build the founder's personal brand in a way that would make the brand more credible, more interesting and more trustworthy to people who had not bought from it yet. Founder-led marketing has a specific dynamic in D2C: when the person behind the product is visible, authentic and specific about why they built what they built, conversion rates improve because trust is higher.

We built a content strategy anchored around her specific founding story: the gap she had identified in the Indian skincare market, the sourcing choices she had made and refused to compromise on, and the ongoing process of building a brand that she would be proud to use herself. The content was specific, personal and unapologetic about the complexity of building a physical product business. It was exactly the kind of content that performs on LinkedIn because it is rare.

Simultaneously, we pitched her story to relevant publications. Within eight months, she had earned three media features and had been invited to participate in two industry panels. The LinkedIn following grew to over 8,000. The founder became a recognised voice in her category, and people increasingly discovered the brand through her story rather than through advertising alone.
LinkedIn Management PR Personal Branding

### Case study: CFO at a mid-cap company, Pune
05 CFO at a mid-cap company, Pune From invisible to a recognised finance voice in eight months LinkedIn Management + Personal Branding 5,200 Followers Built 5,200 Followers Built 8 Months 1 Media Feature
A CFO with eighteen years of experience at two mid-cap listed companies came to us with one specific goal: he wanted to be recognised as a serious, credible voice in corporate finance. He had the credentials and the experience and a track record of taking companies through major milestones. What he did not have was any public presence that reflected the depth of what he knew.

The LinkedIn profile he had when we started said almost nothing useful. It listed companies, titles and dates. It gave no indication of how he thought, what he had built or the depth of judgement he could bring. The About section was two sentences. There were no posts.

We built a content strategy anchored around the topics he knew deeply: governance thinking, capital allocation decisions, reading company financials critically and what makes a CFO genuinely valuable rather than simply accurate. The content was specific, occasionally contrarian and clearly written by someone who had lived the decisions, not just studied them.

We also updated his profile comprehensively, rewrote his headline and About section, and created a Featured section linking to his strongest posts. Within eight months his following grew to over 5,200, and he earned one media feature as an expert voice on corporate governance. He told us the work had changed how senior people in his network perceived him.
LinkedIn Management Personal Branding

### Case study: Legal consultant, Hyderabad
06 Legal consultant, Hyderabad Three times the inbound in six months for an independent practice LinkedIn Management + Content Strategy 3x Inbound Inquiries 3x Inbound Inquiries 6 Months 7,000 Followers Built
A corporate law specialist from Hyderabad had been in independent practice for two years after leaving a mid-size law firm. His primary challenge was not capability. It was that potential clients had no way to evaluate him before a meeting. The referral-based system he was relying on was working, but slowly. The clients he wanted were making decisions based on whoever they had heard of, and he was not in that conversation.

The content strategy we developed was built around the specific needs of his target audience: founders and promoters at growth-stage Indian companies navigating regulatory complexity for the first time. He had seen the same mistakes made dozens of times and had strong views about where founders consistently underestimated legal risk. We turned those views into a regular LinkedIn presence.

The posts he published under our guidance were different from typical legal content on LinkedIn. Rather than regulatory updates or generic compliance advice, they addressed specific scenarios: what happens when a term sheet has a clause the founder did not read carefully, how to structure an ESOP scheme that will not create problems in a future fundraise, what a shareholder agreement needs to say and what gets left out by junior lawyers more often than clients realise. This content was genuinely useful to his target audience and demonstrated expertise in a way that a CV never could.

Within six months, inbound inquiries had tripled. More significantly, the quality of conversations had changed. The people reaching out were coming in already having read his perspective on the specific issue they needed help with. The meetings were shorter and the trust was higher from the first conversation.
LinkedIn Management Content Strategy

### Case study: Tech entrepreneur, Chennai
07 Tech entrepreneur, Chennai Building a credible founder narrative through thought leadership LinkedIn Management + PR + Content Strategy 5,000 LinkedIn Followers 5,000 LinkedIn Followers 3 Months 1 National Media Feature
A second-time founder from Chennai was building a SaaS product for the manufacturing sector. He had a strong technical product and an early customer base. His previous startup had been a modest success and he had learned from it. What he wanted this time was to build his personal profile early, so that the right people in his industry knew his name and his thinking before he ever walked into a room.

The challenge with manufacturing SaaS is that it is a relatively unsexy category from a media perspective. General startup publications tend to focus on consumer tech, fintech and direct-to-consumer brands. Enterprise B2B for manufacturing rarely gets coverage. The strategy therefore had to work at two levels: build a LinkedIn audience among the people who mattered, and find the specific media angle that would earn him a feature.

We built his LinkedIn content around a specific thesis: most manufacturing companies in India are sitting on enormous operational inefficiencies that no consulting firm will ever fix because the solution requires software that did not exist five years ago. He had specific data from his early customers to support this. The content was dense, specific and addressed an audience of manufacturing operations leaders directly. This positioning built genuine credibility with the exact people he most wanted to reach.

The PR work resulted in a media feature covering the industrial technology transformation taking place in Indian manufacturing. The feature positioned him as a founder working on a genuine infrastructure problem rather than a feature-rich tool looking for a market. Within three months of the media work, he had become a recognised name among the operations leaders and industry peers he most wanted to reach.
LinkedIn Management PR Content Strategy

### Case study: SaaS founder, Singapore
08 SaaS founder, Singapore Entering the Indian market with a LinkedIn-first strategy LinkedIn Management + Personal Branding 4,000 India LinkedIn Followers 4,000 India LinkedIn Followers 5 Months India Market Presence Built
A Singapore-based founder of a B2B SaaS company was expanding into the Indian market. Her product had strong traction in Southeast Asia but she had no presence in India, no relationships with Indian enterprise buyers and no media profile in the market she was entering. She needed to build credibility quickly in a new context.

The India LinkedIn audience for enterprise B2B is specific: decision-makers at mid to large Indian companies, technology buyers and the consulting and advisory community that influences their decisions. Building within that audience required a different approach than what had worked for her in Singapore. The content needed to acknowledge the India-specific context, speak to the challenges Indian enterprise operations teams actually face and position her as someone who had done the work to understand the market rather than a foreign founder assuming transferability.

We built a content strategy that combined her genuine expertise in enterprise operations with India-specific research and observations. She wrote, with our guidance, about the specific integration challenges Indian companies face, how procurement cycles work differently in Indian enterprise versus Southeast Asian, and the genuine operational improvements her product category could deliver in an Indian manufacturing or services context. The content was both credible and clearly informed by real knowledge of the local market.

Within five months, she had 4,000 followers in India, the majority of them in her target audience. She told us the LinkedIn presence had made every conversation easier because Indian audiences could see immediately that she had done more than just fly in to pitch.
LinkedIn Management Personal Branding

### Case study: Management consultant, Dubai
09 Management consultant, Dubai From advisory practice to speaking circuit in twelve months LinkedIn Management + PR + Personal Branding 3 Speaking Engagements 3 Speaking Engagements 6,500 LinkedIn Followers 12 Months
A management consultant based in Dubai had left a large firm to set up an independent advisory practice focused on strategy and organisational transformation for regional businesses. He had a strong network from his consulting years and was well-regarded within it. What he wanted was to expand beyond his existing network and break into the regional speaking circuit as a recognised public voice on a specific topic.

His LinkedIn presence when we started was the classic senior consultant profile: extensive, credential-heavy, impressive on paper and utterly uninspiring. It communicated what he had done but nothing about how he thought. His positioning was broad enough to mean nothing. We needed to sharpen both the positioning and the voice significantly.

The content strategy we developed was anchored on a specific tension he had observed repeatedly in regional businesses: the gap between how transformation is sold (as a process, a framework, a methodology) and how it actually works (as a fundamentally human challenge that fails or succeeds based on specific organisational dynamics, not frameworks). He had strong, earned views on this. We turned those views into a consistent, visible public voice.

The PR work focused specifically on the speaking circuit. We built a media kit, pitched him as a speaker and supported three speaking engagements over twelve months. The combination of consistent LinkedIn content and speaking appearances built a compounding visibility effect. By the end of the year he had become a recognised public voice in his field, no longer dependent on his existing network for reach.
LinkedIn Management PR Personal Branding

### Case study: EdTech founder, London
10 EdTech founder, London Breaking into the Indian EdTech market from zero presence LinkedIn Management + PR 2 India Partnerships 2 India Partnerships 3 EdTech Media Features 4 Months
A London-based founder of an EdTech company had built a well-regarded product for corporate learning and development in the UK and European market. She was expanding into India and needed to build both credibility and commercial relationships in a market where she had no existing presence, no media profile and no professional network to speak of.

The India EdTech market has its own specific dynamics. Enterprise L&D buyers in India are influenced by a combination of peer recommendations, industry publications and the personal profiles of the founders they are considering working with. A foreign founder entering this market cold faces a significant credibility gap that no amount of product quality can close on its own. The work needed to happen at the level of positioning and visibility before any commercial conversations could be productive.

We built a LinkedIn content strategy that positioned her as someone who had done the intellectual work of understanding what makes corporate learning actually change behaviour. She had real research and real data on this question from her UK customer base. The content took those findings and applied them specifically to the Indian context: how learning culture inside Indian companies differs from what she had seen in Europe, where the gaps are largest and where the opportunity for impact is highest. The India-specific framing was credible because she had done the homework, and distinctive because most EdTech content is generic by design.

We simultaneously pitched her founder story to relevant publications. Within four months, she had earned three media features. The coverage gave her the credibility shortcut that would have otherwise taken a year of networking to establish. Two Indian corporate L&D partnerships were initiated within the same period, both by organisations that had read her content or seen her profile before reaching out.

About Boldface

# The best people were the hardest to find online.

A LinkedIn studio in Bangalore, running profiles, content and networks for founders and executives across India, Dubai and Abu Dhabi.

Boldface started with one annoying pattern: the people with the best judgement are usually the quietest online. The experience is there. The track record is there. The words aren't.

So we became the people who find the words, and put them in front of the right people. Four years in, that's 35+ founders and executives across India, Dubai and Abu Dhabi, 265K+ followers and 55M+ impressions.

Behind it sits twenty years of brand strategy and 150+ projects across South Asia. But every post still sounds like you, not like us.

01 · Curator & execution lead
### Koushik Agarwalla

Plans, writes and runs every engagement. Three published books, Chief Organiser of TEDxChristUniversity, and four years running LinkedIn for 35+ founders and executives.

Former AVP at Disney Star, Senior Director at Viacom18 and Marketing Head at Radio City. Two decades of brand and storytelling inside India's biggest media houses.

03 · Where the method comes from

Our frameworks come from years of work with Ather, Bacardi, Vini Cosmetics, AJIO, Kuku FM, Cothas Coffee and others across South Asia.

04 · The number behind the number
### 265,000+ followers, and what they led to

Follower counts are the least interesting part. The good bit is the deals, investor messages and invitations that came from the right person reading the right post.

What we believe
The best personal brand in the room isn't the loudest. It's the most honest.

# Page: FAQ | LinkedIn Management Questions | Boldface
URL: https://boldface.online/faq/

FAQ

# What people ask on the first call.

The questions that come up on almost every first call, answered the way we'd answer them across a table.

01

**Q: How quickly will I see results?**

That depends on what you count as results. Engagement and follower growth: four to six weeks. Inbound leads and conversations: usually three to six months. A real change in how your industry sees you: six to twelve months of showing up. If someone promises faster, ask them what they're measuring.

02

**Q: How do you capture my voice?**

We spend the first two weeks on nothing else. A long intake call, a read through anything you've written or said in public, and voice notes of you talking about your topics. Then drafts, back and forth, until you can't tell which ones you wrote yourself.

03

**Q: Do I need to be on LinkedIn every day?**

No. That's the point of hiring us. You join a monthly strategy call, approve posts before they go out and send the occasional voice note. Most clients spend under 30 minutes a week.

04

**Q: Do you message people on my behalf?**

Only the way you would yourself. We build a list of people worth knowing, write personal connection notes and comments, and draft replies for your DMs. You decide how hands-on we get with your inbox. No automation tools and no templates, so nothing ever puts your account at risk.

05

**Q: How is Boldface different from a big agency?**

You work with the founder, not a junior account manager passing notes to a junior writer. And it's all under one roof: big agencies split LinkedIn across a writer, a designer and a social media executive. Here, one team runs your profile, posts, newsletter and network, so they all tell the same story.

06

**Q: Do you work with clients outside India?**

Yes. LinkedIn works the same everywhere, and so do we. Clients today are across [India](https://boldface.online/linkedin-agency/india/), [Dubai](https://boldface.online/linkedin-agency/dubai/) and [Abu Dhabi](https://boldface.online/linkedin-agency/abu-dhabi/), with others in the UK and Singapore.

07

**Q: What does working with you cost?**

There are no fixed packages. A newsletter on its own is a different job from running a CEO's entire LinkedIn plus the company page. We scope it to what you need and price it from there. A 30-minute call gets you a straight number.

08

**Q: What if I want to pause or stop?**

It's a monthly retainer with 30 days' notice. No lock-in, no penalty clauses. If it isn't working, we'd rather hear it on a call than find out when you go quiet. The few clients who've left did so because their business changed, not because the work stopped working.

09

**Q: Can you run LinkedIn for a whole team?**

Yes. We've done it for founding teams and leadership teams, and we run company pages too. Each person gets their own positioning and voice, with a shared story tying them together, so nobody ends up sounding like the comms department.

10

**Q: What should I bring to the first call?**

A rough idea of what you want, and an honest picture of where you are now. No brief, no deck. We'll ask about your goals, your audience and your constraints, and build the plan from there.

11

**Q: Can you set up collaborations and brand deals?**

Yes. We set up co-written posts with peers, guest spots on podcasts and LinkedIn Lives, and joint events. If you have an audience brands want to reach, we source paid partnerships, negotiate them and handle the coordination, so you only show up for the good ones.

Process

# First call to first post in 21 days.

Here's exactly what happens after you say yes, week by week. You'll always know what's next and who's doing it.

21
days from our first call to your first post going live.

Week 01 01
## The intake call

Forty-five minutes on your goals, your audience, your industry, how you talk and what you'd never say. We're learning how you think. You're deciding whether to trust us with your reputation. By the end, we'll both know if it's a fit.

- Day 1-2Intake call booked and done
- Day 3-5We review anything you've written, recorded or said on stage
- Day 6-7First positioning draft lands with you
Week 02 02
## The strategy

We write the plan: what you stand for, the three or four topics you'll own, who you're talking to and a 90-day roadmap. Nothing gets written until you've pushed back on it and signed it off.

- Day 8-10Positioning document drafted
- Day 11-12Content pillars delivered
- Day 13-14Your edits, then final sign-off
Week 03 03
## Profile and first posts

We rewrite your headline, About and Featured sections, then draft four posts that each test a different topic. They're partly about going live and partly about getting your voice exactly right.

- Day 15-17New LinkedIn profile delivered
- Day 18-20First four posts drafted for review
- Day 21Edits done, first posts scheduled
Week 04 onwards 04
## Then it runs

From week four: 8 to 12 posts a month, all approved before they go out. Networking, your newsletter and collaborations run alongside, depending on what you've signed up for. A monthly call keeps us pointed at whatever's working.

- MonthlyNext month's posts approved before it starts
- OngoingNetworking and collaborations with the people on your list
- MonthlyResults review and a plan for the next 30 days

# Page: LinkedIn Profile Optimisation for Founders and Executives | Boldface
URL: https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-profile-optimisation/

[Services](https://boldface.online/services/) / Profile & Positioning

# LinkedIn profile optimisation.

We rebuild your LinkedIn profile around one clear position: what you want to be known for, and who needs to know it. Headline, About, Featured, experience, plus banner and photo direction, all rewritten in your voice. The new profile is usually live within three weeks of the first call.

## Why most founder profiles undersell them

Most LinkedIn profiles read like a CV pasted in a hurry. A job title, a company name, a list of past roles and an About section that opens with “Passionate about”. Nothing on it tells a stranger why they should care.

And strangers are exactly who reads it. Before an investor takes the meeting, before a buyer replies, before an organiser sends the speaking invite, someone looks you up. Your profile is usually the first thing they find, and it does the talking before you get the chance.

## What we rewrite

- Positioning. The one or two things you want to be known for, and the people you want to be known by. Everything else follows from this.

- Headline. What you do, who it's for and why it matters, in a line people actually read.

- About. Written the way you talk, opening with the reader's problem instead of your career history.

- Featured. The three or four things a stranger should see first: a post, a talk, a case study, your newsletter.

- Experience. Outcomes instead of duties, so your track record reads as proof.

- Banner and photo. A clear brief your designer or photographer can work from.

## How it works

It starts with a 45 minute intake call about your goals, your audience and how you talk. We read anything you've written or said in public, draft your positioning and send it over for you to push back on. Once you've signed off the positioning, we rewrite the profile and hand it over ready to go live.

## The first step of everything else

A profile rebuild is the first thing we do for every retainer client, because [posts](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-ghostwriting/) and [networking](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-networking/) work much harder when the profile they lead back to makes sense. If you'd rather do it yourself, start with an [audit](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-audit/): we review your profile and hand you a ranked list of fixes. Our [section by section profile checklist](https://boldface.online/playbook/linkedin-profile-optimisation-checklist/) is free too.

Questions people ask
01

**Q: How long does a LinkedIn profile makeover take?**

About three weeks from the first call. A week to understand you, a week on positioning, and the new profile lands in week three. Most of that time goes into the positioning, because the writing is quick once that's settled.
02

**Q: Will the new profile still sound like me?**

That's the whole job. We work from your intake call, your voice notes and anything you've written, and nothing goes live until you've approved it.
03

**Q: Does profile optimisation help me show up in LinkedIn search?**

Yes. The right terms in your headline and About help people find you in LinkedIn search, and we include them. But a profile stuffed with keywords reads badly to the person who lands on it, so we write for the reader first.
04

**Q: What does a good LinkedIn headline look like?**

It says what you do, who you do it for and what changes for them, in plain words. “Helping D2C brands fix their unit economics” beats “CFO | Strategist | Speaker | Mentor” because a stranger knows instantly whether you're relevant to them.

# Page: LinkedIn Ghostwriting for CEOs and Founders | Content Written in Your Voice | Boldface
URL: https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-ghostwriting/

[Services](https://boldface.online/services/) / Content & Ghostwriting

# Your LinkedIn, written in your voice.

We plan, write, design and publish your LinkedIn content: 8 to 12 posts a month, carousels, short videos cut from your own footage and long-form articles, all in your voice. You approve everything before it goes out. Most clients spend under 30 minutes a week on it.

## What a LinkedIn ghostwriter actually does

The writing is the visible part. Most of the work happens before it: deciding what you should be known for, picking the three or four topics you'll own, and turning your opinions, stories and client conversations into posts people stop for.

A good ghostwriter sounds like you on a good day. We spend the first two weeks of every engagement learning how you talk: an intake call, voice notes, anything you've written or said on stage. Then we draft, you push back, and we keep going until you can't tell which posts you wrote yourself.

## What's included every month

- A monthly content plan and calendar, agreed with you

- 8 to 12 posts a month, written in your voice

- Carousels and document posts

- Short videos edited from footage you shoot on your phone

- LinkedIn articles when an idea needs more room

- Publishing, and a monthly review of what worked and what we change

## Posting more isn't the answer

Plenty of people post every day and get nowhere. The posts that bring in work are specific: a strong opinion about your industry, a decision you'd make differently now, a pattern you've seen across fifty clients. That's what we dig for on the monthly call, which is why your content comes from your thinking and not from a list of trending topics.

## Who it's for

[Founders](https://boldface.online/for/founders/), [CEOs](https://boldface.online/for/ceos/), [CFOs](https://boldface.online/for/cfos/) and [consultants](https://boldface.online/for/consultants/) who have real expertise and no time to turn it into content. Across our clients that has added up to 265K+ followers and 55M+ organic impressions. The numbers that matter more are the meetings, investor messages and invitations that come from the right person reading the right post.

Want to know more before you hire anyone? Read [what a LinkedIn ghostwriter actually does](https://boldface.online/playbook/what-a-linkedin-ghostwriter-does/).

Questions people ask
01

**Q: Is it ethical to use a LinkedIn ghostwriter?**

Yes, as long as the ideas are yours. Speeches, books and op-eds have been ghostwritten for a very long time. We never invent opinions or experiences for you. We take what you actually think and know, and do the writing so it gets out of your head and onto the page.
02

**Q: How many LinkedIn posts should a founder publish a week?**

Two or three good posts a week is enough for most founders, which is why our standard plan is 8 to 12 a month. Consistency over months does far more than a burst of daily posting that stops after three weeks.
03

**Q: Will people know my posts are ghostwritten?**

Not if it's done properly. Every post starts from your own stories, opinions and voice notes, and you approve it before it goes out.
04

**Q: Do you also write LinkedIn articles and newsletters?**

Yes. Articles are part of the content plan when an idea needs more space. A regular newsletter is its own service: see LinkedIn newsletter management.

# Page: LinkedIn Newsletter Management and Writing Service | Boldface
URL: https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-newsletter-management/

[Services](https://boldface.online/services/) / Newsletter Management

# LinkedIn newsletter management.

We run your LinkedIn newsletter end to end: name, format and setup, an editorial calendar, every issue written in your voice and published on schedule, and steady subscriber growth. A newsletter reaches people through notifications and email, which makes it the most reliable way to stay in front of the people who matter.

## Why a newsletter works when the feed doesn't

A post lives in the feed for a day or two and reaches whoever the algorithm decides. A LinkedIn newsletter goes further. Subscribers get a notification and an email when a new issue is out, and when you launch one, LinkedIn invites your network to subscribe.

That makes it the closest thing LinkedIn has to an owned channel. It's also where longer thinking fits: the argument that needs 800 words, your monthly view on the market, the lessons from a deal you just closed.

## What we handle

- Name, format and setup. A name people remember, a format you can keep up, and the newsletter set up on your profile or company page.

- Editorial calendar. Issues planned in advance around your topics, your launches and the questions your audience keeps asking.

- Every issue written and published. In your voice, approved by you, out on the same day every time.

- Subscriber growth. Posts that point to each issue, a Featured slot on your profile, and networking that keeps bringing the right people in.

- Issue by issue review. What got read, what got shared and what we change next time.

## How often should it go out?

Weekly if you have a lot to say and your industry moves fast. Fortnightly or monthly for most founders and executives. The right answer is the frequency you can keep for a year, because a newsletter that goes quiet after issue four does more harm than not having one.

## Personal or company newsletter?

Both work, for different jobs. A newsletter from your personal profile builds trust in you. One from your [company page](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-company-page-management/) builds the brand. Most of our clients start with the personal one. Thinking of starting your own? Read [how to start a LinkedIn newsletter people actually open](https://boldface.online/playbook/how-to-start-a-linkedin-newsletter/).

Questions people ask
01

**Q: Who can start a LinkedIn newsletter?**

Access depends on your account, and LinkedIn changes the rules from time to time. Most personal profiles and company pages can publish one today. We check your account on the first call and tell you exactly what's available.
02

**Q: How long should a LinkedIn newsletter issue be?**

Long enough to say one thing well. Most good issues land somewhere between 600 and 1,200 words. Padding an issue to hit a word count is how newsletters lose readers.
03

**Q: Can you run my newsletter without running my posts?**

Yes. The newsletter can run on its own, though it grows faster when your posts point people to it.
04

**Q: How do you grow LinkedIn newsletter subscribers?**

The launch invite does the early work. After that, growth comes from posts that tease each issue, a link in your Featured section, sharing issues in the right conversations, and networking that keeps adding the right people to your network.

# Page: Strategic LinkedIn Networking for Founders, No Automation | Boldface
URL: https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-networking/

[Services](https://boldface.online/services/) / Strategic Networking

# Strategic LinkedIn networking.

We build a list of the people who matter to you, from investors and buyers to partners and peers, and work it every week: personal connection notes, thoughtful comments on their posts and DM replies drafted for you. No automation tools, no templates, nothing that puts your account at risk.

## Posting gets you seen. Networking gets you in the room.

Most LinkedIn advice stops at content. But a post is a broadcast. Deals, hires and invitations usually come from one to one conversations, and those start long before anyone sends a message.

The way it works is simple. The people on your list keep seeing your name in their comments, saying something useful. By the time your connection request or message arrives, it's from someone they already recognise.

## What we do every week

- Build and keep up a target list: investors, buyers, partners, peers and organisers you'd like to know

- Write personal connection notes, never templates

- Leave thoughtful comments on their posts, in your voice

- Draft replies for your DMs so good conversations don't go cold

- Flag the right moments: a funding round, a new role, a post where you have something real to add

- Report who's new in your network and which conversations turned into meetings

## Why we never use automation

Automation tools send hundreds of identical messages, and people can tell within a line. LinkedIn's user agreement doesn't allow most of them, and accounts that use them get restricted. Your reputation is the whole point of this work, so every note and comment is written by a person who knows your positioning, and you decide how hands-on we get with your inbox.

## Is this lead generation?

Not the cold outreach kind. We don't blast sequences at strangers. It's closer to how a well connected friend would introduce you around: fewer messages, much better conversations. For founders selling high value services or raising money, that's the version that actually works. The thinking behind it is in our guide to [networking on LinkedIn without being that person](https://boldface.online/playbook/linkedin-networking-without-spam/).

Questions people ask
01

**Q: Is LinkedIn automation safe to use?**

We don't think so. LinkedIn's user agreement doesn't allow most third party automation, and accounts that use it can get restricted. It also reads like spam to the people receiving it. Everything we do is done by hand.
02

**Q: How many people do you reach out to each week?**

It depends on your goals and how much of your inbox you want us to handle. A short list of the right people, worked consistently, beats hundreds of requests to strangers.
03

**Q: Can LinkedIn networking help me raise funding?**

It helps with the warm part. Investors who have seen your thinking for months take meetings more easily, and a good network makes warm introductions easier to ask for. It won't replace a strong business, but it makes sure the right people already know who you are.
04

**Q: What's the difference between networking and content?**

Content is one to many. Networking is one to one. Content earns attention and networking turns specific people into relationships. They work best together, which is why we run them under one plan.

# LinkedIn collabs, Lives and events.

We put you in front of audiences that already trust someone else: co-written posts with peers, guest spots on podcasts and LinkedIn Lives, LinkedIn events of your own and, when brands want your audience, paid partnerships we source and negotiate. You show up for the good ones. We handle the rest.

## The fastest way to grow is someone else's audience

Growing from your own posts alone is slow. A collaboration puts you in front of people who already follow a peer, a podcast host or an event, and they arrive half convinced because someone they trust brought you in.

## What we set up

- Co-written posts. Posts written with respected peers in your industry and shared with both audiences.

- Podcast and LinkedIn Live guest spots. We find shows your buyers actually follow, pitch you, and prepare you for the conversation.

- Your own Lives, audio events and LinkedIn Events. Planned, promoted and run, so all you do is turn up and talk.

- Brand partnerships. If brands want to reach your audience, we source paid partnerships, negotiate them and handle the coordination.

## Picking the right ones

A big audience in the wrong industry is worth less than a small one full of your buyers. Every collaboration we bring you gets checked against one question: will the people watching be the people you want to know? Sandeep Komarla, our brand strategy advisor, spent two decades inside Disney Star, Viacom18 and Radio City and has 75+ strategic partnerships behind him. Every collaboration we broker goes past him first.

## Brand deals without the awkwardness

Paid partnerships damage trust when they don't fit. We only bring you brands that make sense for your audience, write the posts so they sound like you, and say no on your behalf to the ones that don't.

Questions people ask
01

**Q: How do founders get invited onto podcasts?**

Have a clear point of view, make it easy for hosts to see it, and pitch shows whose audience matches yours. Your LinkedIn does a lot of the work here, because hosts look you up before they say yes.
02

**Q: What is a LinkedIn Live, and do I need one?**

A LinkedIn Live is a live video broadcast on your profile or page, with comments coming in as you talk. You don't need one to grow, but for founders who are good on camera it's a strong way to turn followers into people who feel they know you.
03

**Q: How do LinkedIn brand partnerships work?**

A brand pays you to create posts that reach your audience. We find the brands, check they fit, negotiate the fee and terms, and handle the coordination. You approve every post.
04

**Q: Do collaborations work for B2B founders?**

Often better than for consumer brands. B2B buyers trust peers, so a joint post with a respected operator or a guest spot on an industry podcast carries a lot of weight.

# LinkedIn company pages and teams.

We run your LinkedIn company page and get your leadership team posting alongside it, each person in their own voice, all telling one story. Employees can join in with posts we make easy to share. People follow people before they follow logos, so we grow the page through the people behind it.

## Why company pages struggle on their own

A company page matters: it's where candidates, buyers and investors go to check you're real. But on its own it rarely travels far in the feed, because people engage with people far more than with brands. The pages that grow have a leadership team behind them, sharing and adding their own view.

## What we run

- Company page content: launches, hiring, culture, customer stories and point of view posts

- Page cleanup: About, tagline, visuals briefed, and Showcase pages where they make sense

- Leadership team profiles and posts, each with its own positioning

- Employee posts made easy to share, so your team can join in without writing from scratch

- One editorial plan across the page and every leader's account

## Leadership teams, not just the founder

When a CEO, a CFO and a CTO each post about what they actually know, the company starts to look like a team worth working with, not a logo with a careers page. We've run LinkedIn for founding teams and leadership teams, and each person gets their own voice, so nobody ends up sounding like the comms department.

## Employee advocacy, minus the cringe

Most employee advocacy programmes fail because they ask people to reshare corporate posts word for word. We do it differently: short, optional prompts and drafts people can make their own, so what goes out sounds like a person and not a press release. Not sure where your effort should go first? Read [company page or personal profile: where should founders post?](https://boldface.online/playbook/company-page-vs-personal-profile/)

Questions people ask
01

**Q: Should a founder post from the company page or a personal profile?**

Mostly the personal profile. People engage with people, so a founder's posts usually reach far more than the company page does. Use the page for official news, hiring and proof, and let the founder and leadership team carry the point of view.
02

**Q: How often should a company page post on LinkedIn?**

Two to four times a week suits most companies, as long as each post is worth reading. A page with three great posts a week beats a busy one nobody engages with.
03

**Q: What is employee advocacy on LinkedIn?**

Your employees sharing and talking about the company on their own profiles. Done well, it reaches far more people than the company page can alone, because each employee brings their own network.
04

**Q: Can you manage just the company page?**

Yes, though it works far better alongside the founder and leadership team. If you only want the page, we'll still plan it around the people in the company.

# LinkedIn audits and workshops.

If you'd rather run LinkedIn yourself, start here. We audit your profile and content and hand you a written fix list ranked by impact, or train your leadership team in a single working session. One sharp outside view, no monthly retainer.

## What the audit looks at

- Positioning. Is it obvious what you're known for, and to whom?

- Profile. Headline, About, Featured, experience, banner and photo.

- Content. Your recent posts: what worked, what didn't, and why.

- Network. Whether the people you want to reach are actually in it.

- Rhythm. How often you show up, and whether you can keep it up.

## What you get

A written fix list, ranked by impact, so you know exactly what to change first. Not a forty page deck. The top few fixes are usually things you can do in an afternoon, and they tend to make the biggest difference.

## Workshops for leadership teams

One working session for your leadership or founding team. We cover positioning, profiles and how to write posts that sound like a person, then work on real profiles and drafts during the session. Everyone leaves with a sharper profile and a plan they can actually keep.

## When an audit is the right call

An audit suits people who write well, have the time and just need an outside eye. If you know you won't find the time every week, a [monthly retainer](https://boldface.online/services/linkedin-ghostwriting/) is the better fit, and the audit becomes its first step. Want a head start? Work through our [profile optimisation checklist](https://boldface.online/playbook/linkedin-profile-optimisation-checklist/) first.

An outside review of your LinkedIn profile, content and network against what you want to achieve, with a clear list of what to fix. Ours comes as a written fix list ranked by impact.

Leadership and founding teams who want to show up on LinkedIn themselves but need a shared approach. It's also a good first step before a company wide employee advocacy push.

# LinkedIn for CFOs and finance leaders.

# LinkedIn for consultants and advisors.

Yes, carefully. Sharing knowledge and commentary is generally fine, while soliciting work or advertising services can break professional rules. We keep content educational and opinion led.
03

For B2B consulting, almost always. Your buyers are on LinkedIn in a work frame of mind, and thoughtful long-form posts travel well there.
